note: This is a REVIEW ARTIFACT, not an auto-merge, mirroring the existing convention in mrsilent_bridge/discovery_data/ and the explicit rule in mrsilent_bridge/capability_registry.py: 'nothing in this project auto-registers a capability without a human having reviewed and added a JSON entry.' Originally written 2026-09-02T00:25 by the OMNISIM_OMNI_ORACLE_GOD_MODE_V1 campaign; refreshed 2026-09-02T01:30 (RESUME_OMNISIM_OMNI_ORACLE_FINAL_INTEGRATION campaign) to correct now-stale claims (the underlying engines were unseeded-random when this was first written; they are deterministic as of commit f313b50) and to add an explicit review_determination per this round's instruction to determine what requires Founder/human approval vs. what may be safely integrated under existing policy.

review_determination.question: What requires Founder/human approval versus what may be safely integrated under existing policy?
review_determination.answer: 100% requires human review before merge. mrsilent_bridge/capability_registry.py's own docstring states this as an unconditional rule with no carve-out: 'Read-only at runtime: nothing in this project auto-registers a capability without a human having reviewed and added a JSON entry (or run organ_discovery.py, whose output is a review artifact, not an auto-merge).' There is no 'safe to auto-integrate' tier in the existing policy -- every entry in mrsilent_bridge/registry_data/capabilities.json (35 as of this writing, re-verified live 2026-09-02) was added this way. Live registry_search/capability_status still return zero matches for 'omnisim'/'oracle' as of this writing.
review_determination.recommendation: A human copies the two proposed_entries below into capabilities.json's entries array if satisfied with the evidence_basis cited for each. Neither entry grants execution/production/financial authority (risk_class=decision_support_only_no_execution_authority on both) -- merging the registry entry only makes the capability discoverable via registry_search/capability_status, it does not by itself wire MCP routing (see services/th3_mcp/tools.py status separately) or grant any protected-gate action.

proposed_entries.purpose: Governed what-if / decision-support scenario analysis via 3 transparent heuristic/arithmetic engines (decision_heuristic, resource_model, comparative_scenario). Not a predictive model.
available_actions: request_scenario(question, assumptions=None, options=None, *, scenario_type=..., variables=..., constraints=..., requested_outputs=...)
proposed_entries.io_contract: in: question (str) + scenario_type + variables/constraints (dict); out: structured result with scenario_outputs, uncertainty, risks, limitations, receipt path
proposed_entries.cost_class: free_local (pure Python, no external calls, no paid compute)
proposed_entries.validation_method: omnisim/tests/test_request_scenario.py (4/4 passing, independently re-run 2026-09-02); live systemd timer omnisim-loop.timer
known_callers: services/th3_mcp/tools.py (hardcoded direct import, not via this registry, as of 2026-09-02)
proposed_entries.evidence_basis: omnisim/reports/omnisim_v1_certification_20260831.json (self-reported, disclaimer-qualified) + independent re-run of its test suite across all 4 campaign sessions (2026-09-02) + live canary via divisions/omnioracle/api/request_oracle.py's also_run_omnisim_scenario ensemble path
